Rashi on Menachot 93b:10:1.hebrew: דקאי להדי רישיה - בשוה הראש, אימא לא נמעט:
Rashi on Menachot 93b:10:1.english: Which is level with its head - Level with the head; I would say let us not exclude [it].

Rashi on Menachot 93b:12:1.hebrew: על הצדדין - של ראש, על הלחיים:
Rashi on Menachot 93b:12:1.english: On the sides - Of the head, [i.e.,] on the cheeks.

Rashi on Menachot 93b:13:1.english: What is the law regarding whether it interposes - Between his hand and the [animal's] head.

Rashi on Menachot 93b:14:1.english: It is written: “His hand” [yado] - [It is spelled] defectively [without the second yod].

Rashi on Menachot 93b:15:1.hebrew: אקפד - על שלא אמרה משמו. ואקשי ליה: אי ס"ד וכו', למה לי דכתב רחמנא בשום מקום בתורה ידיו מלא? לכתוב ידו, ומשמע נמי תרי:
Rashi on Menachot 93b:15:1.english: Took offense - Because he did not state it in his name. And he raised an objection to him: If it enters your mind, etc., why did the Merciful One need to write yadav in plene anywhere in the Torah? Let it write yado, and it would also mean two!

Rashi on Menachot 93b:17:1.hebrew: ידו דסמיכה קאמרי - דמשמע תרי, והא לא אשכחן ידיו מלא דסמיכה:
Rashi on Menachot 93b:17:1.english: I was speaking of the “his hand” of semikhah - That it implies two [hands], since we do not find “his hands” [written] plene with regard to semikhah.

Rashi on Menachot 93b:18:1.english: I was speaking of placing hands on an animal - For wherever “his hand” [yado] is stated, it implies two [hands].

Rashi on Menachot 93b:19:1.hebrew: (מאי) קאמר - במקום שסומכין שוחטין, כלומר: דלאחר שסומכין לאלתר שוחטין, שתכף לסמיכה שחיטה, דהכי מסתבר שפיר. (ע"א) מאי קאמר: דמשמע ליה דבאותו מקום בבהמה שסומכין שם שוחטין, והלא אין סמיכה בצואר? נ"ל:
Rashi on Menachot 93b:19:1.english: (What) is it saying - "In the place where they lean, they slaughter" — that is to say, immediately after they lean, they slaughter, because slaughter immediately follows leaning, for this makes good sense. (Another explanation) "What is it saying?": Because it understood it to mean that on that same place on the animal where they lean, there they slaughter — and yet, leaning is not done on the neck? So it seems to me.

Rashi on Menachot 93b:19:2.hebrew: במקום שסומכין - בעזרה במקום הטבעות, דבשעת סמיכה היו ישראל רשאין ליכנס שם:
Rashi on Menachot 93b:19:2.english: In the place where they lean - In the Courtyard, at the place of the rings, for at the time of leaning, Israelites were permitted to enter there.

Rashi on Menachot 93b:1:1.hebrew: דנין קרבן יחיד מיחיד - מעולת ראייה, דהוי נמי קרבן יחיד:
Rashi on Menachot 93b:1:1.english: We derive an individual offering from an individual [offering] - From the pilgrimage burnt offering, which is also an individual offering.

Rashi on Menachot 93b:1:2.hebrew: דנין - סמיכה בקרבן יחיד, דכתיב ביה סמיכה בגופיה, דכתיב "וסמך", מפר העלם דבר של ציבור, דכתיב ביה סמיכה בגופיה: "וסמכו זקני העדה" (ויקרא ד׳:ט״ו):
Rashi on Menachot 93b:1:2.english: One derives - [The requirement of] placing hands on an individual's offering, concerning which placing hands is written in its own passage, as it is written: “And he shall place [his hand]” — from the bull brought for an unwitting communal sin, concerning which placing hands is written in its own passage: “And the elders of the congregation shall place [their hands]” (Leviticus 4:15).

Rashi on Menachot 93b:3:1.hebrew: לימד על עולת חובה - כגון האי דמילואים, ועולת ראייה כמו עולת חובה היא:
Rashi on Menachot 93b:3:1.english: Teaches about an obligatory burnt offering - Such as this one of the inauguration, and a burnt offering of appearance is like an obligatory burnt offering.

Rashi on Menachot 93b:5:1.english: Why do I need all these - And could not all of these be excluded from a single [mention of] "his hand"?

Rashi on Menachot 93b:5:2.hebrew: ושלוחו של אדם כמותו - דגמרינן (קדושין דף מא:) מפסח, דכתיב ושחטו אותו כל קהל וגו':
Rashi on Menachot 93b:5:2.english: And a person's agent is like himself - For we derive (Kiddushin 41b) from the Paschal offering, as it is written: "And the whole assembly of the congregation [of Israel] shall slaughter it" etc.

Rashi on Menachot 93b:7:1.hebrew: (סמיכה שירי מצוה - שאם לא עשאה, לא מעכב):
Rashi on Menachot 93b:7:1.english: Placing hands is a non-essential mitzvah - That if one did not perform it, it does not prevent [atonement].

Rashi on Menachot 93b:7:2.hebrew: כאילו לא כיפר - כאילו לא עשה מצוה מן המובחר, כדכתיב (ויקרא א) וסמך ונרצה. ואפילו הכי כיפר, דכפרה בדם הוא:
Rashi on Menachot 93b:7:2.english: As if he did not effect atonement - As if he did not perform the mitzvah in the optimal manner, as it is written (Leviticus 1): “And he shall lay [his hand] and it shall be accepted.” And even so, he effected atonement, for atonement is through the blood.

Rashi on Menachot 93b:9:1.hebrew: ולא על הצואר - היינו הגרון, בית השחיטה:
Rashi on Menachot 93b:9:1.english: And not on the neck - That is, the throat, the place of slaughter.

Rashi on Menachot 93b:9:2.english: The back - That is, the back.

Tosafot on Menachot 93b:4:1.hebrew: ידו ולא יד אשתו - מהא דכתיב "בני ישראל" למעוטי נשים מסמיכה, לא נפקא אשתו, דהוה אמינא תסמוך בקרבן בעלה, דכיד בעלה דמיא. וא"ת: ולמה לי קרא למעוטי נשים מסמיכה? תיפוק לי דמצות עשה שהזמן גרמא, אם תכף לסמיכה שחיטה דאורייתא, כדאמר בפ' כל הפסולין (זבחים לג.) דאפילו סמך בסוף הלילה תכף לעמוד השחר, צריך לשחוט עדיין את התמיד תחילה, שלא יהא דבר קודם לתמיד! עוד תנן בפרק ב' דמגילה (דף כ:): כל היום כשר לסמיכה ולשחיטה; דריש בגמרא דכתיב "ביום זבחכם", ואיתקש סמיכה לשחיטה, דכתיב ושחט וסמך:
Tosafot on Menachot 93b:4:1.english: His hand, and not his wife's hand - From that which is written, "the sons of Israel" (Leviticus 1:2), to exclude women from semikhah, his wife would not be excluded; for I might have thought that she may perform semikhah on her husband's offering, since she is considered like her husband's hand. And if you say: But why do I need a verse to exclude women from semikhah? Let it be derived from the fact that it is a positive time-bound commandment [from which women are exempt] — if [the rule that] slaughter must immediately follow semikhah is Biblical, as the Gemara says in the chapter "Kol HaPesulin" (Zevachim 33a): that even if one performed semikhah at the end of the night immediately adjacent to the dawn, he must still slaughter the daily morning offering first, so that nothing precedes the daily offering! Furthermore, we learned in the second chapter of Megillah (20b): "The entire day is valid for semikhah and for slaughtering" — and the Gemara expounds that it is written: "on the day of your sacrifice" (Leviticus 19:6), and semikhah is juxtaposed with slaughtering, as it is written: "and he shall lay his hand... and he shall slaughter" (Leviticus 1:4–5).

Tosafot on Menachot 93b:7:1.hebrew: כאילו לא כיפר וכיפר - בפ"ק דזבחים (דף ו.) בעי למידק מהכא, דלא מכפר אעשה דלאחר הפרשה, דקאמר: מאי לאו, כיפר עשה דקודם הפרשה, לא כיפר סמיכה, דהוה ליה עשה דלאחר הפרשה? ואמר רבא: עשה דסמיכה קאמרת? שאני הכא, כיון דכל כמה דלא שחט בעמוד וסמוך קאי, אימת קא הוי עשה? לאחר שחיטה, חשיב כעשה דלאחר שחיטה. אמר ליה רב הונא בר (רבי) יהודה לרבא: ואימא כיפר גברא, לא כיפר קמי שמיא, כדתניא: והנותר בשמן אשר על כף הכהן כו'. ותימה, דלא מייתי מברייתא דתנופה דהכא, דעל כרחין לא כיפר קמי שמיא קאמר, דלא שייך למימר לא כיפר עשה, דתנופה היא לאחר זריקה! ויש לומר, דהך ברייתא מיתניא גבי אשם מצורע בתורת כהנים, שטעון תנופה חי, ושייך לפרש: לא כיפר עשה דתנופה מחיים:
Tosafot on Menachot 93b:7:1.english: As though he did not atone, and yet he atoned - In the first chapter of Zevachim (6a), [the Gemara] seeks to deduce from here that [an offering] does not atone for [the violation of] a positive commandment [committed] after designation. For [the Gemara] says: What, does it not mean that it atoned for a positive commandment [violated] before designation, but did not atone for [the positive commandment of] semikha (laying on of hands), which is a positive commandment [violated] after designation? And Rava said: Are you speaking of the positive commandment of semikha? It is different here, since as long as he has not slaughtered [the animal], he stands under [the continuing obligation of] "arise and perform semikha." When does it become [a violation of] a positive commandment? After slaughter! [Therefore,] it is considered like a positive commandment [violated] after slaughter. Rav Huna bar [Rabbi] Yehuda said to Rava: But say that it atoned for the person, [yet] it did not atone before Heaven, as it is taught [in a baraita]: "And the rest of the oil that is on the priest's palm, etc." And this is difficult: why did [the Gemara] not bring proof from the baraita of tenufah (waving) taught here [on our daf]? For there, perforce, it must mean "it did not atone before Heaven," since it is not applicable to say that "it did not atone" refers to the positive commandment [of waving], given that tenufah is performed after the sprinkling [of the blood]! And one can say that this baraita is taught in Torat Kohanim regarding the guilt-offering of a leper, which requires waving while alive; and [thus] it is applicable to explain: it did not atone for the positive commandment of waving while alive.

Tosafot on Menachot 93b:9:1.hebrew: ולא ידו על הצואר - לצד הגרון, מקום הסימנין, ששם קרוי צואר, כדתנן בפרק קמא דחולין (דף יט:):
Tosafot on Menachot 93b:9:1.english: And not his hand on the neck - [This means] toward the side of the throat, the location of the *simanim* [the organs of slaughter], for that [area] is called "neck," as we learned in the first chapter of Chullin (19b).
